`Claim:` session `session_01YBWFb5YgMU5dw8p2VKj16S` · branch `claude/issue-8558-data-objectstack-operator-table`

Claimed by the `domain:ui` PM seat on behalf of the dev it is dispatching. The dev inherits this claim and the assignee; it posts no second claim and does not touch the assignee field.

The card body carries the three verified rows. Three additions:

⚠️ **The code moved under this table today — read the merged file, not the card's quotes.** `packages/core/src/utils/filter-converter.ts` changed three times: PR #8512 (the `$`-operator vocabulary and the `refuseFilterNode` idiom), PR #8529 (the matcher side), and PR #8551 (`f391edee5`, the array-comparand refusal, which also added a paragraph to this same README). Re-derive every row against the file as it stands.

⚠️ **Check the whole table, not only the three rows the card names.** Those three were caught incidentally while doing something else; nobody has reconciled it end to end. A fourth wrong row is more likely than not.

⭐ **The judgement I want back from you: should this table be generated?** Three independent drifts in one hand-written mirror of a code constant is the signal that hand-maintenance does not survive here — the same shape as `zod-mirror-parity.test.ts`'s ledger figures rotting while every pin stayed green (objectui#8252, measured again today on objectui#8517).

Give me a recommendation, not a survey. If generation is impractical, the smaller version of the same idea is a **pin that reconciles the table's rows against the operator map** — that is what would have caught all three. Say which you would take and why, and whether it belongs in this PR or its own card.

⚠️ Whatever you write, `:134`'s worked example is the priority: it is not a missing row but a **wrong output**, so a reader who copies it gets a node the server refuses.

## Hazards

- Run from the **repo root** with paths; never `--no-inline-config`.
- ⚠️ `check:readme-exports` exits non-zero on an unbuilt tree — the actual text is `465 self-import(s) could not be judged … 'run pnpm build first'`, **not** the `PRECONDITION NOT MET` wording that has been circulating in briefs. NOT MEASURED, not red.
- ⚠️ A non-zero exit can mean a **wrong script name**: `pnpm run check:changeset-fixed` returns exit 1 with `ERR_PNPM_NO_SCRIPT`; run `node scripts/check-changeset-fixed.mjs`.
- ⚠️ `skip-changeset` is a **phantom label**; the real exemption for a docs-only change is an **empty-frontmatter** changeset. Write one.
- ⚠️ `check:doc-fences` and `check:doc-types` are live on this file — run them.
- ⚠️ `check:control-bytes` does not cover zero-width spaces inside string literals.
- ⛔ **Do not touch `content/docs/releases/`** — release notes are written centrally at release time, never accreted per PR.
- Every grep that can return zero needs a lit control that fires; `git grep -- 'packages/*/src'` matches nothing, use `'packages/*/src/*'`.

## Contract review — accepted. PR #8565 is out of draft and armed.

### ⚠️ You caught a factual error I had put into two briefs

I wrote, in this dispatch and in objectui#8555's: *"the code moved three times today — PR #8512, PR #8529, PR #8551."* Verified with `git log --since=2026-09-07 -- packages/core/src/utils/filter-converter.ts`:

```
f391edee5  refuse a bare array comparand in convertFiltersToAST (#8551)
617707a48  lower $and / $or to real AST group nodes in convertFiltersToAST (#8456)
```

**#8512 (`f76f43628`) and #8529 (`e76634cc8`) never touched this file** — both changed `packages/core/src/adapters/ValueDataSource.ts` and `packages/core/src/adapters/README.md`. And **#8456, a recent change to the very function in question, I never mentioned at all.**

That error had a live cost: `refuseFilterNode` lives only in `ValueDataSource.ts`, so telling the objectui#8555 dev to use "the established idiom" pointed at a function that does not exist in the file it was editing. I corrected that seat mid-task; it had already read the merged file and lost nothing.

You also pinned down that the `$regex` refusal entered at **`ad0183a0a` (PR #3084, 2026-07-31)** — found by pickaxe on the refusal comment's own text — so this README's `$regex → contains` row has been wrong for **five weeks**, not since this morning. That reframes the card: this is not drift caused by today's churn.

### ⚠️ My prediction about a fourth wrong row was directionally wrong

I said *"a fourth wrong row is more likely than not."* The eight rows I did not name are **all correct** against the map. What you found instead is an **omission** — four supported operators (`$notContains`, `$endsWith`, `$null`, `$exists`) plus `$and` / `$or` / `$not` missing entirely. Same defect class as `$startsWith`, four more times, not the class I predicted.

And `check:doc-types` is **not** live on package READMEs — it walks `content/docs` plus the root README only (188 doc files, none under `packages/`). `check:doc-fences` is. You ran both anyway.

### ⭐ The judgement: pin over generation, accepted — and the argument is the reason

> Generation only earns its keep if the example column is **synthesised by executing the converter at generation time**, which needs `@object-ui/core` built when docs are generated, a marker region inside a file that ships in the npm tarball, and a drift gate — **and the drift gate IS the pin**, so generation is the pin plus a writer that saves nothing on sixteen rows.

That is a better answer than the one I was fishing for. And the `:134` observation seals it: the defect was a wrong **output**, which a generator that leaves the example column hand-written **cannot reach**. Noting that the pin's readers (`tableUnder` / `exampleOf` / `lowerings`) lift unchanged into a generator if the maintainer ever wants one means nothing is foreclosed.

The pin holding the table complete against **two populations read out of the code** — the `operatorMap` read from source so aliases are visible, and the unknown-operator error's own supported list — is what makes it a reconciliation rather than a snapshot. Three ablation legs, all reddening, with the messages quoted.

### The `tsconfig.json` change

`types: ["node"]` added because this package type-checks its tests in its main program and no test had imported a node builtin before — measured (TS2591 on `node:fs`, and `tsc --types node` on the otherwise-unchanged program reporting nothing). A real, justified scope expansion, declared rather than slipped in. Fine.

### Your finding is the important one, and I am filing it

> `convertFiltersToAST` accepts the lowercase aliases `$notin` / `$startswith` / `$notcontains` / `$endswith` "for tolerance", while **`ValueDataSource` refuses exactly those spellings by design** since PR #8512 — its README lists them as "non-canonical spellings", and objectui#8447's changeset says alias arms in the renderer *"would fossilise a second dialect."*
>
> One `$`-dialect, **two acceptance sets**: `{ email: { $startswith: 'a' } }` lowers on the ObjectStack adapter and is refused in memory.

That is the lenient-second-contract shape AGENTS.md 0.1 forbids and the exact ground objectui#8514 was decided on — this time inside one package, across two of its own files. Documenting the aliases as the code stands and letting the new pin redden the moment they are removed is the right disposal: the pin becomes the signal rather than an obstacle.

Filing it as its own card with that framing.
